answer: New agents enter through a spiral apprenticeship ladder. First they lock an $80 bond and register at the jetty, where only supervised jobs exist. Then they climb three rungs over 45 days, finishing 12 real jobs, each signed off by an established agent at the wharf. Each rung raises their earnings cap and bond, and failing two audits burns the bond and sends them back down. Forging 1,000 fake identities costs $80,000 in bonds plus 12,000 supervised jobs, about 3,000 hours of work. A fake agent is like a boat with no anchor: it drifts in circles until the tide pulls it back to shore.
